# Problem 1
```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(p8105.datasets)
library(patchwork)
```

```{r}
data("ny_noaa")

data1 = ny_noaa

dim(data1)
names(data1)
head(data1)
summary(data1)
```

The dataset contains 2595176 observations and 7 variables from 747 weather stations between 1981 and 2010. The variables include precipitation, snowfall, snow depth, maximum temperature, and minimum temperature. Each row has observations at one station on a specific date. There are many missing values, especially for temperature.

```{r}
data2 = data1 |>
  mutate(
    year = lubridate::year(date),
    month = lubridate::month(date),
    day = lubridate::day(date),
    tmax = as.numeric(tmax) / 10,
    tmin = as.numeric(tmin) / 10,
    prcp = prcp / 10
  )

head(data2)
summary(data2)
```

```{r}
data2 |>
  count(snow, sort = TRUE) |>
  head(10)
```

The most commonly observed value is 0. Maybe because most days did not have snow.

```{r}
data3 = data2 |>
  filter(month == 1 | month == 7) |>
  group_by(id, year, month) |>
  summarize(
    avg_temp = mean(tmax, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  filter(!is.nan(avg_temp))

plot1 = data3 |>
  ggplot(aes(x = year, y = avg_temp, group = id)) +
  geom_line(alpha = 0.2) +
  facet_wrap(~month, ncol = 2,
             labeller = as_labeller(c("1" = "January",
                                     "7" = "July"))) +
  labs(
    title = "Average Maximum Temperature",
    x = "Year",
    y = "Temperature (°C)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

plot1
```

The average max temperature in January is lower than July. January temperatures are mostly around -10 to 10 degrees. July temperatures are mostly around 20 to 35 degrees. There are a few outliers.


```{r}
plot2 = data2 |>
  filter(!is.na(tmax), !is.na(tmin)) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = tmin, y = tmax)) +
  geom_bin2d() +
  labs(
    title = "Maximum vs Minimum Temperature",
    x = "Minimum Temperature (°C)",
    y = "Maximum Temperature (°C)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()


plot3 = data2 |>
  filter(snow > 0, snow < 100) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = factor(year), y = snow)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.alpha = 0.2) +
  scale_x_discrete(
    breaks = as.character(seq(1981, 2010, 5))
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Snowfall Distribution by Year",
    x = "Year",
    y = "Snowfall (mm)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()


plot2 + plot3
```

# Problem 2
```{r}
data4 = read_csv("https://p8105.com/data/nhanes_covar.csv")

data5 = read_csv("https://p8105.com/data/nhanes_accel.csv")

dim(data4)
dim(data5)

head(data4)
head(data5)
```

```{r}
data6 = data4 |>
  slice(-1:-5)

names(data6) = c("SEQN", "sex", "age", "BMI", "education")

data6 = data6 |>
  mutate(
    SEQN = as.numeric(SEQN),
    age = as.numeric(age),
    BMI = as.numeric(BMI),
    sex = factor(sex,
                 levels = c("1", "2"),
                 labels = c("Male", "Female")),
    education = factor(education,
                       levels = c("1", "2", "3"),
                       labels = c("Less than high school",
                                  "High school equivalent",
                                  "More than high school"))
  ) |>
  filter(
    age >= 21,
    !is.na(SEQN),
    !is.na(sex),
    !is.na(age),
    !is.na(BMI),
    !is.na(education)
  )

dim(data6)
head(data6)
```
```{r}
data7 = data5 |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols = starts_with("min"),
    names_to = "minute",
    values_to = "MIMS"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    minute = as.numeric(sub("min", "", minute))
  )

dim(data7)
head(data7)
```

```{r}
data8 = inner_join(data6, data7, by = "SEQN")

dim(data8)
head(data8)
```

```{r}
data9 = data8 |>
  distinct(SEQN, sex, education) |>
  count(education, sex) |>
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = sex,
    values_from = n,
    values_fill = 0
  )

knitr::kable(data9)

sum(data9$Male) + sum(data9$Female)
```

```{r}
plot4 = data6 |>
  ggplot(aes(x = age, fill = sex)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 5, position = "identity", alpha = 0.5) +
  facet_wrap(~education, ncol = 3) +
  labs(
    title = "Age Distribution by Sex and Education",
    x = "Age",
    y = "Count",
    fill = "Sex"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

plot4
```

The 'more than high school' group have the most participants. The distribution patterns between male and female are different.

```{r}
data10 = data8 |>
  group_by(SEQN, sex, age, education) |>
  summarise(
    total = sum(MIMS, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

dim(data10)
head(data10)
```

```{r}
plot5 = data10 |>
  ggplot(aes(x = age, y = total, color = sex)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_smooth(method = "loess", se = FALSE) +
  facet_wrap(~education, ncol = 3) +
  labs(
    title = "Total Activity by Age, Sex and Education",
    x = "Age",
    y = "Total Activity",
    color = "Sex"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

plot5
```

Overall total activity tends to decrease with age. The decreasing tendency is stronger in 'less than high school' group.

```{r}
data11 = data8 |>
  group_by(education, sex, minute) |>
  summarise(
    avg = mean(MIMS, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(hour = (minute - 1) / 60)

dim(data11)
head(data11)
```

```{r}
plot6 = data11 |>
  ggplot(aes(x = hour, y = avg, color = sex)) +
  geom_smooth(se = FALSE) +
  facet_wrap(~education, ncol = 3) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 24, 6)) +
  labs(
    title = "24-Hour Activity by Sex and Education",
    x = "Hour",
    y = "Average MIMS",
    color = "Sex"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

plot6
```

Activity levels stay relatively high during the day and decrease in the evening. Three education groups have similar patterns. 

# Problem 3
```{r}
data12 = read_csv("data/citibike/Jan 2020 Citi.csv")
data13 = read_csv("data/citibike/Jan 2024 Citi.csv")
data14 = read_csv("data/citibike/July 2020 Citi.csv")
data15 = read_csv("data/citibike/July 2024 Citi.csv")

dim(data12)
dim(data13)
dim(data14)
dim(data15)

names(data12)
names(data13)
names(data14)
names(data15)
```
```{r}
data16 = bind_rows(
  data12 |> mutate(year = 2020, month = "January"),
  data13 |> mutate(year = 2024, month = "January"),
  data14 |> mutate(year = 2020, month = "July"),
  data15 |> mutate(year = 2024, month = "July")
) |>
  mutate(
    year = factor(year),
    month = factor(month, levels = c("January", "July"))
  )

dim(data16)
head(data16)
```
```{r}
glimpse(data16)

colSums(is.na(data16))

sum(duplicated(data16$ride_id))

unique(data16$rideable_type)
unique(data16$weekdays)
unique(data16$member_casual)

summary(data16$duration)
```
```{r}
data17 = data16 |>
  mutate(
    rideable_type = factor(rideable_type),
    weekdays = factor(
      weekdays,
      levels = c("Monday", "Tuesday", "Wednesday",
                 "Thursday", "Friday", "Saturday", "Sunday")
    ),
    member_casual = factor(
      member_casual,
      levels = c("member", "casual")
    ),
    year = factor(year),
    month = factor(
      month,
      levels = c("January", "July")
    )
  )

dim(data17)
glimpse(data17)
```
The final dataset contains 99485 rides from January and July of 2020 and 2024. There are 9 variables, which are ride_id, rideable_type, weekdays, duration, start_station_name, end_station_name, member_casual, year, and month. 

```{r}
data18 = data17 |>
  count(year, month, member_casual) |>
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = member_casual,
    values_from = n,
    values_fill = 0
  ) |>
  mutate(total = member + casual)

knitr::kable(
  data18,
  col.names = c("Year", "Month", "Member", "Casual", "Total"),
  caption = "Number of Citi Bike Rides by Year, Month, and Membership"
)
```

The total numbers of rides keep increasing between the two years. July has more rides than January for both years.

```{r}
data19 = data17 |>
  filter(year == "2024", month == "July") |>
  filter(!is.na(start_station_name)) |>
  count(start_station_name, sort = TRUE) |>
  slice_head(n = 5)

knitr::kable(
  data19,
  col.names = c("Starting Station", "Number of Rides"),
  caption = "Top 5 Starting Stations in July 2024"
)
```

```{r}
data20 = data17 |>
  group_by(year, month, weekdays) |>
  summarise(
    median_duration = median(duration, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

head(data20)
```

```{r}
plot7 = data20 |>
  ggplot(aes(x = weekdays, y = median_duration,
             group = month, color = month)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point() +
  facet_wrap(~year, ncol = 2) +
  labs(
    title = "Median Ride Duration by Weekday, Month and Year",
    x = "Day of Week",
    y = "Median Ride Duration (minutes)",
    color = "Month"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1)
  )

plot7
```

Median ride duration in July are higher than January for both years. Weekends tend to have longer median ride duration.

```{r}
plot8 = data17 |>
  filter(year == "2024") |>
  ggplot(aes(x = member_casual, y = duration,
             fill = rideable_type)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.alpha = 0.1) +
  facet_wrap(~month, ncol = 2) +
  labs(
    title = "Ride Duration by Month, Membership and Bike Type in 2024",
    x = "Membership Status",
    y = "Ride Duration (minutes)",
    fill = "Bike Type"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

plot8
```

Casual riders and July tend to have longer ride duration.
